grammar_rule.title: Telling Time
grammar_rule.explanation: In Irish, to tell the time, you use 'Tá sé' (It is) followed by the number for the hour. For half past, you use 'leathuair' (half an hour). For minutes past the hour, use 'a' before the number of minutes.
examples: Tá sé a dó a chlog. (It is two o'clock.)
Tá sé leathuair tar éis a haon. (It is half past one.)
Tá sé a deich a chlog. (It is ten o'clock.)

pronunciation_notes: Practice the pronunciation of numbers 1-10 for accuracy.
Pay attention to the slender and broad vowels in Irish words.
Listen to native speakers for correct intonation and rhythm.

grammar_rule.title: Using 'agam', 'agat', 'aige', etc.
grammar_rule.explanation: In Irish, possession is indicated by using 'agam' (at me), 'agat' (at you), 'aige' (at him), 'aici' (at her), etc. before the possessed item.
examples: Tá cat agam. (I have a cat.)
Níl carr agat. (You don't have a car.)
Tá madra aige. (He has a dog.)

pronunciation_notes: 'agam' is pronounced 'ah-gum'
'agat' is pronounced 'ah-gut'
'aige' is pronounced 'egg-eh'
